value: Arizona has used a FLAT 2.5% individual income tax rate for all filing statuses since tax year 2023 (SB 1828 phase-down completed early due to revenue triggers), unchanged for 2025 and 2026 — this is the lowest flat rate of any state that levies a broad individual income tax. UNIQUE MECHANISM: Arizona withholding is NOT bracket-based; instead each employee ELECTS a flat PERCENTAGE OF ARIZONA GROSS TAXABLE WAGES to be withheld via Form A-4 ('Arizona Withholding Percentage Election'). For 2025 the selectable percentages are 0.5%, 1.0%, 1.5%, 2.0%, 2.5%, 3.0%, or 3.5% (unchanged from 2024), or the employee may elect zero withholding if eligible. If a new employee does not submit a Form A-4 within 5 days of hire, the employer must withhold at the DEFAULT rate of 2.0% until an election is made. Arizona has NO local/municipal income taxes (state law preempts cities/counties from levying one). Arizona has reciprocity with California, Indiana, Oregon, and Virginia via Form WEC.

value: CT's headline bracket rates for 2024 onward are 2%, 4.5%, 5.5%, 6%, 6.5%, 6.9%, 6.99% (the two lowest brackets were cut from 3%/5% to 2%/4.5% by 2023 legislation effective tax year 2024, per CT Office of Legislative Research report 2025-R-0080). NOTE: this is commonly referred to informally as the '3% phase-out,' but since the 2024 rate cut the lowest bracket is actually 2%, so DRS now formally calls this the '2% Tax Rate Phase-Out Add-Back' (Table C) — it recaptures the benefit of the 2% bracket (vs. the next-higher 4.5% rate) for taxpayers above set AGI thresholds, adding back up to $250 (single/MFS), $500 (MFJ), or $400 (HOH). SEPARATELY, CT also has a 'Tax Recapture' (Table D) that claws back the benefit of ALL the lower brackets for high earners, capping out at a recapture add-back of $3,400 (single/MFS), $6,800 (MFJ), or $5,320 (HOH) at sufficiently high AGI. CT also has a Personal Exemption (Table A) that phases out with AGI: max exemption $15,000 (single) / $24,000 (MFJ) / $12,000 (MFS) / $19,000 (HOH), phasing to $0 by AGI of $44,000 / $71,000 / $35,000 / $56,000 respectively. Finally, a Personal Tax Credit (Table E, a percentage applied to reduce tax) also phases out with income. Brackets, exemption, phase-out, and recapture tables are CONFIRMED IDENTICAL for tax years 2025 and 2026 — DRS Informational Publication IP 2026(1) explicitly states 'The 2026 withholding calculation rules and 2026 withholding tables are unchanged from 2025.'

value: Act 46, Session Laws of Hawaii 2024 (signed by Gov. Green 6/3/2024), is a multi-year, multi-stage individual income tax cut running from tax year 2024 through 2031. It widens the income tax bracket thresholds in tax years 2025, 2027, and 2029 (rates themselves stay 1.40%-11.00%; only the dollar thresholds at which each rate applies increase) and raises the standard deduction in tax years 2024, 2026, 2028, 2030, and 2031. Because the two changes alternate by year, TAX YEAR 2026 USES THE SAME BRACKET THRESHOLDS AS TAX YEAR 2025 (next bracket widening is 2027) but a substantially higher standard deduction than 2025 (next standard-deduction increase after 2026 is 2028). CAUTION: Hawaii's Booklet A payroll WITHHOLDING formula tables are a simplified approximation that stops increasing the withholding rate at 7.9% for annualized wages above $125,000 (single) / $250,000 (married) -- they do NOT include the 8.25%/9.00%/10.00%/11.00% brackets that apply to actual tax liability on Form N-11. The brackets recorded in this fragment are the full statutory Tax Rate Schedules from the Form N-11 instructions (used to compute actual liability), not the abbreviated withholding-table brackets; a payroll withholding calculator should still use the Booklet A withholding formula/tables for per-paycheck withholding, but true tax liability calculations must use the full 12-bracket schedule shown here.

value: All 92 Indiana counties impose a local income tax (LIT) on county adjusted gross income, withheld by employers alongside the flat state tax. The applicable county rate is based on the employee's Indiana county of RESIDENCE as of January 1 of the tax year (not county of employment); if the employee resides out-of-state on Jan 1 but has a principal place of work/business in an Indiana county as of Jan 1, that county's rate applies instead. Rates are published twice yearly (Jan. 1 and Oct. 1) in DOR Departmental Notice #1.
